title: When the Mixtape Wakes
premise: Odile Reyes, a closeted debate champion hiding behind perfect grades, discovers his late grandmother's recipe box holds spellwork — instructions for a magic of voice and memory that the town's founding families have quietly hoarded for generations. When his best friend Marisol is targeted by a binding charm meant to erase her family's claim to their home, Odile must master the recipes while competing in the state debate championship, where the mayor's son, Theo Calloway, wields stolen spells as persuasion. The final round becomes a duel disguised as a debate: Odile wins not by out-arguing Theo but by breaking his power's source and speaking the truth no charm can silence. In the end, he loses the trophy but wins back the neighborhood, comes out to his family, and claims his grandmother's legacy as keeper of the recipes.
about_author: Mirabel Brightwater grew up in a border town where every kitchen smelled like someone else's grandmother's cooking, and she never stopped believing recipes could be spells. She writes young adult stories about kids who find their voices in the last place anyone thought to listen.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. We meet him mid-debate season: flawless on stage, silent at home where his father dismisses everything he says. He deflects Marisol's questions about why he never speaks up at school board meetings about her family's threatened eviction. Emotional beat: the ache of being articulate everywhere except where it counts.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Sorting his grandmother Abuela Luzia's belongings, he finds the recipe box: cards for arroz con pollo, yes, but also cards titled 'To Loosen a Tongue' and 'To Remember What Was Taken.' The handwriting shifts from ink to something darker that moves when he isn't looking. Beat: wonder laced with dread.

chapters.title: First Taste
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following 'To Loosen a Tongue' half-skeptically, he bakes pan dulce that makes his taciturn father talk for an hour about grief and Odile's mother leaving. Terrified and exhilarated, Odile realizes the recipes work — and that Abuela Luzia knew exactly what she was doing. Beat: vertigo of inherited power.

chapters.title: Marisol's Notice
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Her family receives a final eviction notice backed by a land claim from the Calloway Development Group. She vents to Odile, who almost tells her what he found but swallows it. Beat: the cost of secrets between best friends.

chapters.title: The Calloway Boy
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At a pre-tournament mixer, Theo Calloway is magnetic — everyone agrees with him before he finishes sentences. Odile recognizes the recipe box's telltale shimmer around Theo's words. Someone else has been cooking. Beat: cold recognition that he's not the only one.

chapters.title: Card by Card
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He deciphers more recipes: protections, bindings, one card scorched nearly blank labeled only 'Do Not.' His tía Rosa catches him and goes pale, revealing Abuela Luzia left the box to whoever 'the town needs next.' Beat: legacy becomes obligation.

chapters.title: Practice Round
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Debate regionals: Odile wins cleanly without magic, proving to himself he still can. But afterward Theo compliments him with unsettling precision, quoting Odile's private thoughts. Beat: pride shadowed by surveillance.

chapters.title: What the Town Forgot
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Researching the land claim, she finds records that literally don't exist — pages missing, memories fuzzy, elders suddenly unsure their families ever owned anything. She suspects tampering but can't prove it. Beat: gaslighting made municipal.

chapters.title: The Scorched Card
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Under lamplight and salt, he recovers the burned card: 'To Take a Voice,' the recipe Theo's family used to build their fortune — and the one Abuela Luzia died trying to destroy. Beat: horror at how deep the corruption runs.

chapters.title: Allyship, Awkwardly
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Odile finally confesses everything to Marisol; furious, then fierce, she becomes his strategist. They test counter-recipes together in her kitchen, laughing for the first time in chapters. Beat: trust rebuilt into partnership.

chapters.title: Midterms and Middle Ground
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. His father discovers the missing pan dulce ingredients and accuses him of lying; the argument explodes into Odile coming out before he planned to. His father walks out. Beat: the home argument he can't win — yet.

chapters.title: Theo's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Inside the Calloway house: Theo's father forces him to cook obedience charms, punishing failure. Theo hates it and does it anyway. He notices someone else's magic in town. Beat: villain revealed as another trapped kid.

chapters.title: The Binding on Barrio Lane
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. On eviction day, Marisol's abuela can't remember her own address — a binding charm in action. Odile counters with 'To Remember What Was Taken,' and the whole block remembers at once, singing their deeds aloud. Beat: collective memory as resistance.

chapters.title: Retaliation
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Mr. Calloway strikes back: Odile's scholarship is mysteriously revoked, Marisol's mother fired. The recipes protected them once; now the enemy plays by institutional rules too. Beat: power corrupts through paperwork as much as spellwork.

chapters.title: Stealing Back the Box
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The pair infiltrate Calloway Hall during a gala and discover the source: the original recipe book, chained in the study, feeding the family's charms. Theo catches them — and lets them go, shaken. Beat: the enemy cracks open.

chapters.title: Theo Defects
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo copies three cards and leaves them in Odile's locker with a note: 'He's renewing the Voice-taking at the championship finals. Whole town will be there.' Beat: betrayal of blood for conscience.

chapters.title: Losing on Purpose
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Semifinals: Odile throws his match to stay under the radar, and it costs him — the crowd, his coach, his own pride. Marisol reminds him which championship matters. Beat: sacrifice reframed as strategy.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Odile and Marisol prepare the counter-recipe — 'To Give a Voice Back' — requiring a true name spoken freely. His father returns, quietly, having read Abuela Luzia's letters; he offers his name first. Beat: reconciliation without easy forgiveness.

chapters.title: Finals
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. State championship, packed auditorium, Mr. Calloway renewing the great charm from the balcony. Odile faces Theo across the podium, both boys speaking double meanings while the audience feels its memories thinning. Beat: two duels in one room.

chapters.title: The Argument That Matters
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Mid-round, Odile abandons his case and speaks plainly: names the charm, names the thefts, invites the town to say its own name back. The counter-recipe ignites through the crowd; the great charm shatters; Mr. Calloway's power collapses mid-word. Beat: truth as the winning argument.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Measured in Recipes
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Investigations begin; deeds restored; Theo testifies against his father, hollowed but free. Odile loses the title on a technicality and doesn't care. The barrio cooks together, every pot a small spell of belonging. Beat: justice outside the law, warmth after fire.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Box
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Epilogue: Odile adds his first new card to the box — 'To Begin Again' — and places it beside Abuela Luzia's. His father asks him to teach him one. Head up now, voice loud, he writes. Beat: inheritance accepted, story complete.
